title: Bonang
summary: The bonang is a rack of small kettle gongs set in two rows on cords stretched across a wooden cradle. Struck with two padded sticks, it plays the bright melody that leads a Javanese gamelan.
howToPlay: Ten kettle gongs are lit: five Low in front, five High behind.
A ring closes on the gong to strike. The padded stick visits it and the bronze rings.
The pitch climbs from left to right along each row.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Each kettle gong rests on cords, so it rings freely. Players answer one another across the two rows, one hand on each row.
credits: Tradition: the bonang of Javan gamelan; patterns written for this game
